text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, A02 dispatches about 50 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A03 (about 43 in 100 before) and only about 21 in 100 to A04 (about 31 in 100 before), while the share going to A07 edges up from about 20 to 22 in 100; A02 itself also recurs more often (about 1.9 versus 2.2 occurrences per trace on average). [DIR002, OCC001]
- A03 and A17 always occur together — A03 is virtually always followed by A17 — and in the later window they appear in about 54 in 100 traces versus about 47 in 100 before; they also repeat more within a case (about 2.3 occurrences per trace versus 1.5, with repeats in about 48 versus 33 in 100 of the traces containing them). [OCC002, OCC016, DIR003, REL045]
- The pair A04/A14, which likewise always occurs together, appears in about 48 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 60 in 100 before. A04 and A07 never share a trace and together cover every trace; their split moves from about 60/40 favouring A04 to 48/52 favouring A07 (A07: 40% → 53% of traces). The mirror-image pair A12/A14 moves from about 40/60 to 52/48, with A12 always travelling alongside A07 and A14 alongside A04. [OCC003, OCC006, OCC011, OCC013, REL048, REL055, REL086, REL123]
- Activities lying after these routes appear in more traces in the later window: A15 from about 22% to 38%, A11 from 18% to 27%, A05 from 29% to 41%, A10 from 30% to 35%, A06 from 32% to 37%, and A08 and A09 rise slightly (to 25% and 33%). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC014]
- Within the branches, two secondary shifts appear: from A17, the share continuing to A05 rises from about 43% to 50% while A06 falls from about 28% to 23%; from A07, the share going to A15 rises from about 20% to 30% while A09 falls from about 30% to 20%. [DIR005, DIR009]
- A04 and A13 sit at later relative positions in the later window (median position 0.73 → 0.80 for A04, 0.68 → 0.76 for A13), and A14 tends to lie farther after A02 (about 75% → 59% of pairs two steps away, 23% → 33% four steps away). [POS004, POS012, LAG030]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, execution is redistributed between the existing branches at the A02 branch point: A02 leads more often into the A03→A17 loop, which also repeats more per case, and less often into the A04/A14 branch, flipping the mutually exclusive choice between the A04 route and the A07 route (which always includes A12) from roughly 60/40 to 48/52; consequently A05, A06, A07, A08, A09, A10, A11, A12 and A15 appear in a larger share of cases while A04 and A14 appear in a smaller share. Supporting signs are the direct shift in A02's outgoing shares, the mirrored participation changes of A03/A17 versus A04/A14, the clean flips in the strict-alternative pairs A04/A07 and A12/A14, and consistent co-occurrence changes with A01 (up for A03, A07, A11, A12, A15 and A17; down for A04 and A14). One limitation is that the A03/A17 increase comes mostly from more repetitions per case rather than more distinct cases, so the change combines re-routing with a more frequently repeated loop. [DIR002, OCC002, OCC003, OCC006, OCC010, OCC011, OCC013, OCC016, REL002, REL003, REL006, REL010, REL011, REL013, REL014, REL048, REL123]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is ordinary sampling variability between the two 200-trace windows, since no baseline is provided for how many qualifying items an unchanged process would produce; against this, the key differences all point in one coordinated direction across the occurrence, direction, relation and position indicators and rank in the top few percent of random re-splits. [DIR002, OCC003, OCC016, REL048]

Other differences: A17 continues to A05 more often and A07 continues to A15 rather than A09, with A15 in turn leading to A11 slightly more often (about 46% → 53%); A04 and A13 occur at later relative positions and A14 tends to lie farther after A02 in the later window. [DIR005, DIR008, DIR009, POS004, POS012, LAG030]
